title: Other token sampling methods: greedy, top-k, and top-p

cues.en: Torched.
cues.zh: torch.

cues.en: Multinomial is a popular method for selecting tokens because it's simple and intuitive, but it's not the only method.
cues.zh: multinomial 是常見的 token 選擇方法，簡單、直觀，但不是唯一方法。

cues.en: So in this video, I will introduce you to three more ways to pick a token.
cues.zh: 這支影片，再介紹三種挑 token 的方式，

cues.en: Once we have a probability distribution over all the possible tokens.
cues.zh: 前提是，已有所有可能 token 的機率分布。

cues.en: So by the end of this video you will have seen four methods for picking a token the probability selection from the previous video, and the three you'll learn here.
cues.zh: 看完後，會知道四種：上一支的依機率選擇，以及這裡三種。

cues.en: And these are not all of the methods.
cues.zh: 還不是全部，

cues.en: There's also like ancestral and beam and other methods.
cues.zh: 也有 ancestral sampling、beam search 等其他方法。

cues.en: But that's fine.
cues.zh: 但沒關係，

cues.en: All the probabilistic methods are reasonably similar to each other.
cues.zh: 這些機率式方法，大致相似。

cues.en: Imagine you have given these words to the model, and the model is trying to predict a word to fill in the blank here.
cues.zh: 假設給模型這些字，要預測一個字，填入空格。

cues.en: And now imagine that these are the five tokens with the highest probabilities.
cues.zh: 再假設，這五個 token 的機率最高，

cues.en: And yeah so these are their probabilities.
cues.zh: 這些就是機率。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: That's the setup.
cues.zh: 情境如此。

cues.en: The greedy selection method just picks the top probability token.
cues.zh: 貪婪選擇，直接挑機率最大的 token。

cues.en: It doesn't matter what the actual probability value is as long as it's the highest.
cues.zh: 不在意機率實際多少，只要最高。

cues.en: So in this case, that seems fine.
cues.zh: 這個例子，看起來沒問題，

cues.en: Seems like coffee.
cues.zh: 似乎 coffee，咖啡，

cues.en: Here is the clear winner.
cues.zh: 明顯勝出。

cues.en: But in this distribution, all of these tokens have a fairly similar probability.
cues.zh: 但另一個分布，各 token 機率相當接近，

cues.en: And yet the greedy selection technique would still always pick coffee.
cues.zh: 貪婪方法，仍永遠選 coffee。

cues.en: Without exception, every single time you present these words to the model, it will always pick coffee.
cues.zh: 每次給模型這些字，都會選 coffee，

cues.en: No exception.
cues.zh: 沒有例外。

cues.en: By the way, in case you are summing up these numbers, doesn't matter that they don't add to one.
cues.zh: 順帶一提，如果你在加數字，沒加到 1，沒關係。

cues.en: There's like 50,000 other tokens over here that can sum up to 5%.
cues.zh: 其他大約五萬個 token，還能合計佔 5%。

cues.en: Okay, the greedy algorithm is deterministic and so it can be pretty boring.
cues.zh: 貪婪演算法是確定性的，所以可能很無聊。

cues.en: A model with a greedy token selection might sound repetitive.
cues.zh: 用這種方法，模型聽起來可能重複，

cues.en: It might even get stuck on one token and just repeating that token over and over again.
cues.zh: 甚至卡在同一 token，一直重複。

cues.en: You can contrast that with the top k algorithm.
cues.zh: 再看 top-k。

cues.en: So here the idea is to sort all of the probabilities and pick one at random from the top k, where k is the parameter, and it's just some number of tokens.
cues.zh: 先排序全部機率，再從前 k 個隨機挑一個；k 是參數，代表 token 數。

cues.en: So in this case k equals three.
cues.zh: 這裡 k 等於 3，

cues.en: And any of these tokens could be picked at random.
cues.zh: 這幾個都有可能被隨機選中。

cues.en: It would be impossible for the model to pick pocket even though its probability is very close to mouth.
cues.zh: 即使 pocket 的機率和 mouth 很接近，也不可能選到 pocket。

cues.en: Here is another example with k equals two.
cues.zh: 另一例，k 等於 2，

cues.en: So now the model can only make two possible choices for this token.
cues.zh: 這個 token 只有兩種可能選擇。

cues.en: But it is a little weird to have the model with a 50 over 50 shot at picking either of these tokens, considering the huge difference in the probabilities.
cues.zh: 不過，兩者機率差那麼多，卻各有一半機會，有點奇怪。

cues.en: So with top k, the parameter is the number of tokens.
cues.zh: 所以，top-k 的參數，是 token 數，

cues.en: It doesn't matter what the actual probabilities are, we're just selecting the top top k tokens.
cues.zh: 不在意實際機率，只選前 k 個。

cues.en: You can contrast that with top p.
cues.zh: 再比較 top-p。

cues.en: So this is a similar idea, except now you pick a summed probability cutoff and you pick randomly from
cues.zh: 概念類似，但先定累積機率門檻，再從

cues.en: however many tokens it takes to get to that probability.
cues.zh: 達到門檻所需的那些 token 中，隨機挑選。

cues.en: So let's say we set the probability cutoff to be 0.98 or 98%.
cues.zh: 假設門檻是 0.98，也就是 98%。

cues.en: How many tokens does it take to get to 98%?
cues.zh: 幾個 token，才累積到 98%？

cues.en: Well, in this case it takes four tokens.
cues.zh: 這裡需要四個，

cues.en: So now the model would pick one of these.
cues.zh: 所以，模型會選其中一個。

cues.en: So this distribution here has only one token that exceeds the probability value.
cues.zh: 這個分布，只有單一 token，就超過門檻，

cues.en: So this is the only token that can possibly be selected in this case.
cues.zh: 因此，只可能選它。

cues.en: So you can see that top p is a bit of a balance between top k and greedy.
cues.zh: top-p 有點像 top-k 與貪婪法之間的平衡。

cues.en: Because this selection method would act like greedy when the model is highly certain about one specific
cues.zh: 模型對某個特定 token，非常有把握時，

cues.en: token, and top P would act more like top K when the model is more uncertain and activates lots of tokens
cues.zh: 會像貪婪法；比較不確定，讓很多 token 都可能

cues.en: for potentially being the next one.
cues.zh: 成為下一個時，則更像 top-k。

cues.en: There's no single best method for picking tokens.
cues.zh: 沒有單一最好的 token 選擇方法。

cues.en: If you want to have an informal social chat with a model, then it's nice to have a bit more randomness
cues.zh: 想和模型輕鬆聊天，可以多一點

cues.en: in the token selection so that the model doesn't sound stiff and repetitive.
cues.zh: 隨機性，避免僵硬、重複。

cues.en: On the other hand, if you're using an LLM to help you code or draft some kind of technical or legal
cues.zh: 但若用 LLM 協助寫程式，或起草技術、法律

cues.en: document, you don't want it to go off the rails and just start giving you random snippets of code that are only loosely related to your actual goal.
cues.zh: 文件，就不希望它失控，開始給只和目標稍有關係的隨機程式片段。

cues.en: Likewise, if you want to use ChatGPT to help you write a children's story, then some unexpected plot twists can be really fun and clever.
cues.zh: 同樣，用 ChatGPT 寫兒童故事，一些意外轉折，可以很有趣、有創意。

cues.en: But if you're trying to get accurate historical information, you really don't want the model to start making a bunch of random claims that just aren't true.
cues.zh: 但想取得準確歷史資訊，就不希望模型隨意編出不真實的主張，

cues.en: Because the actual true token wasn't selected just because of a probabilistic selection method.
cues.zh: 只因機率式選擇，沒有選到真正正確的 token。

cues.en: So this is a real issue that remains unresolved.
cues.zh: 這確實是尚未解決的問題。
